quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Use your mirrors. You do not need to look over your shoulder unless you notice something unusual.
Either use your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Make sure no other drivers are in your way.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery and dangerous. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest position.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not ride between rows of stopped or slowly moving vehicles. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to operate safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign has white background with red and black markings. It means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car. It puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing to be more visible to other drivers. This helps reduce your risk of a collision. Always watch the other drivers around you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: Pointed with your toes aiming downward.

questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Make sure your motorcycle is in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral indicator light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet during a crash is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as a rider without a helmet.
More likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders wearing helmets are three times more likely to survive head injuries than riders without helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and is operated by the rider's left foot.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface coming up.
Conditions that do not change as you get closer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not change as you get closer.
questions.explanation: Look for problems on the road that could create risks. Make a plan to reduce those risks.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, helmets are:
questions.explanation: You must wear a helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation any time you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For people 21 and older, it is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. For people under 21, the limit is 0.01 percent. Even below the legal limit, it may not be safe to operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: You should check your motorcycle before every ride. This quick inspection only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to make your motorcycle visible to other drivers. Always make sure your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: How should you sit to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily use all controls. Bend your arms slightly and use them to steer, not to support your weight. Press your knees against the tank to help you stay balanced during turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the right lane will end.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Prevent eyeglasses or sunglasses from being worn.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your vehicle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Position your vehicle closest to the traffic control device.
Position your vehicle at the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your vehicle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane that puts you in another driver's view as soon as possible.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:

options.text: A test of the turn signals.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The bike has less traction for stopping when it is leaning.
The rider is focused on the turn and not on braking.
The brakes do not work when the bike is turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike has less traction for stopping when it is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. While the motorcycle is leaning to turn, some traction is used for the turn, leaving less traction available for stopping.

questions.question: A "wobble," or sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake from side to side. Most wobbles are caused by improper weight distribution, unsuitable add-ons, or incorrect tire pressure.
